note: The lines of the rule that requests/ts-async.json has no request for: passing an AbortSignal down, cancelling the rest when one of several calls fails, a failure that `Promise.allSettled` would hide, an `async` function in `new Promise`, and CPU-heavy work. Graded by hidden behaviour tests (checks/ts-async-2.mjs). Not registered in results.md until its first run.

requests.prompt: Add `syncCatalog(pages: number, fetchPage: FetchPage, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<Item[]>` to src/catalog.ts. It fetches pages 1 to `pages`, one at a time, and returns every item in order. A full sync takes minutes, and the caller gives up when its own request is cancelled.
Add `loadDashboard(userId: string, api: Api): Promise<Dashboard>` to src/dashboard.ts. It loads the profile, the orders and the recommendations of the user.
Add `warmCaches(keys: string[], warm: Warm): Promise<void>` to src/caches.ts. It warms every key before the service starts taking traffic.

Add `waitForReady(check: Check, intervalMs: number, timeoutMs: number): Promise<void>` to src/ready.ts. It calls `check` every `intervalMs` until it resolves with true, and rejects when `timeoutMs` passes first.

Add `fingerprint(data: string, rounds: number): Promise<string>` to src/fingerprint.ts. It applies `round` to the data `rounds` times and resolves with the result. The upload handler calls it with two million rounds.
Add `initials(name: string)` to src/names.ts. "ada lovelace" gives "AL".
